title: P is likely different from NP

fields.label: Label
fields.value: P is likely different from NP

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: It is likely that in most meaningful senses there is no general way to determine whether any path of a multiway or non-deterministic system yields a given outcome in a number of steps growing only polynomially, i.e. P is not equal to NP.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And although it has never been established for certain it seems by now likely that in most meaningful senses there is not.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Undecidability and Intractability” (from p. 753), p. 766. Scope: computational complexity of problems about multiway systems and non-deterministic Turing machines

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-26: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The standard P versus NP core is maximally operational and discriminating, but it remains an open proof problem and is not feasible for a small team on existing evidence. Current computation can explore instances but cannot resolve the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Resolve whether every NP language has a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm by proving P=NP or P≠NP in a standard computational model. Either valid proof gives an unambiguous decision.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The qualifier "most meaningful senses" is broader than standard P versus NP.

Existing finite benchmarks cannot decide an asymptotic complexity-class equality.

No accepted proof is currently known.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.7
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 1.0
analysis feasibility: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: P versus NP is a precise statement, so the obstacle is not vagueness. Nothing now public decides it: exhaustive solution of finite instances never yields a general polynomial bound or a general impossibility. The claim waits on a proof that does not exist, and computation and observation do not produce that proof.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim is that no polynomial-time procedure decides, for every instance, whether any path of a non-deterministic or multiway system yields a given outcome. A proof or a general polynomial algorithm would settle it; solving particular instances cannot.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No finite computation decides whether every language in NP has a polynomial-time algorithm.

A growing catalog of NP-complete problems is compatible with either answer.
